newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Vodni Stavby says wins rail tender.
newsitem.headline: Czech Vodni Stavby says wins rail tender.

text.p: Czech builder Vodni Stavby a.s. said on Friday it won a tender as the main supplier for a 969 million crowns ($35.8 million) order to build part of a high speed railway corridor for Czech Railways.
Vodni's Trade Director Karel Biskup said his firm would supply 45 to 50 percent of the total amount.
"We are doing all the engineering works between (the northern city of) Decin and the border with Germany," Biskup told Reuters.
The construction should be finished in 1998, he added.
The high-speed railway corridor will connect Germany and Vienna through Prague and Brno in the Czech Republic.
Vodni Stavby is listed on the main market of the Prague Stock Exchange. Its net profit rose to 170 million crowns last year from 120 million in 1994.
